title: Join Us
text: We are building a collaborative and interdisciplinary team, and we are excited to hear from researchers and students interested in developing computational approaches to understand cancer.

title: Join Us
text:
Research scientist
We currently have an opening for a Research Scientist with a strong computational background. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in:

Python programming and Linux/Unix environments
Image processing, computer vision, and deep learning
Computational pathology and digital pathology image analysis
Spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, or other multi-omics data
Multimodal machine learning and image–omics integration
High-performance or GPU computing and reproducible computational workflows

Experience in every area is not required. We particularly value strong computational fundamentals, rigorous problem-solving, scientific curiosity, and the ability to learn new methods independently.

title: Join Us
text:
Postdoctoral fellows and students
We also welcome inquiries from prospective postdoctoral fellows and students whose interests align with the lab. Because our research is highly computational, applicants should have a quantitative or computational background. Prior experience in computational pathology or cancer research is welcome but not essential for candidates with strong computational foundations and an interest in learning the biology.
We are especially interested in people who enjoy working across disciplinary boundaries, developing rigorous computational methods while engaging deeply with the biological and clinical questions that motivate them.

title: Join Us
text:
How to apply
All interested candidates should email Xiaoxi at xiaoxi.pan@hci.utah.edu with the following materials:

A cover letter to describe your research interests and why you are interested in our lab
Your CV with links to GitHub, Hugging Face, publications, if available

Applicants are encouraged to highlight experience with Python, Linux, computer vision/image processing, computational pathology, spatial omics, and/or multi-omics analysis.
If our research interests align, we would be very happy to hear from you.

title: Research
text: We connect tissue structure, cellular neighborhoods, and molecular measurements to understand cancer. Our research focuses on three complementary themes: (1) AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis, (2) multimodal integration of radiology, pathology, and omics data, and (3) the effects of inhaled pollutants on the tumor microenvironment and treatment response in lung cancer, particularly in never-smokers.

title: Research
section: AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis
text:
AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis
We develop computational pathology models for tissue segmentation, histologic pattern classification, and cell-level phenotyping, and apply them to large clinical cohorts. These models quantify tumor architecture, cellular composition, morphology, spatial organization, and microenvironmental heterogeneity, enabling studies of survival in lung cancer, treatment response in triple-negative breast cancer, and cancer progression in Barrett’s esophagus.

title: Research
section: Multimodal integration across imaging and molecular data
text:
Multimodal integration across imaging and molecular data
We integrate pathology with radiology, spatial transcriptomics, and other molecular data to connect imaging phenotypes with cellular and molecular states across spatial scales. By jointly modeling tissue morphology, radiologic features, gene expression, and spatial context, we aim to define clinically relevant tumor phenotypes and improve biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and outcome prediction.

title: Research
section: Pollutant-associated tumor microenvironments in lung cancer
text:
Pollutant-associated tumor microenvironments in lung cancer
We study how inhaled pollutants, including tissue-resident particulate matter (PM), reshape the tumor microenvironment in lung cancer, with a particular focus on never-smokers. By combining AI-based pollutant mapping with spatial transcriptomics and cellular-resolution analysis, we investigate pollutant-associated immune and stromal states, their relationship to tumor progression, and whether these microenvironmental changes influence response to systemic therapy.

title: Pan Lab
text:
Xiaoxi [shyow-shee]

 xiaoxi.pan@hci.utah.edu

 GitHub  Google Scholar  LinkedIn

Huntsman Cancer Institute
Department of Oncological Sciences
University of Utah





I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Oncological Sciences and Huntsman Cancer Institute at the University of Utah. My research program develops computational approaches using artificial intelligence (AI) that transform routinely collected pathology specimens into quantitative representations of tumor biology and integrates these features with omics and clinical data to answer clinically and biologically meaningful questions.
Prior to joining the U, I was working as an Instructor and then a principal data scientist in the lab led by Dr. Yinyin Yuan at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center (2023 to 2026). I completed my postdoctoral training in Dr. Yuan’s lab at the Institute of Cancer Research (ICR), UK (2020 to 2023), and I received my Ph.D. in Optics, Photonics and Image Processing at Ecole Centrale Marseille, France (2016 to 2019).
I am actively looking for talented students and postdocs as founding members of Pan Lab! See how to join the lab.
